questions.stem: Ultrafiltration of blood in the kidney takes place in the
questions.explanation: Blood enters the glomerulus through a wide arteriole and leaves through a narrower one, which raises the pressure and forces small molecules out through the capillary wall into the Bowmans capsule. Blood cells and plasma proteins are too large to pass and remain in the blood.

distractorRationale.b: The loop of Henle creates the salt gradient used to conserve water
distractorRationale.c: The collecting duct carries out the final water reabsorption under ADH control
distractorRationale.d: The ureter merely conveys finished urine to the bladder

questions.stem: Which substance present in the glomerular filtrate is normally completely reabsorbed before the urine leaves the kidney?
questions.explanation: Glucose is far too valuable to waste, so carrier proteins in the proximal convoluted tubule return every molecule of it to the blood by active transport. Urine from a healthy person therefore contains no glucose, and finding glucose there is a standard test for diabetes mellitus.

distractorRationale.a: Urea is a waste product and is deliberately left in the filtrate
distractorRationale.c: Much water is reabsorbed but never all of it, since some is needed to carry the urea away
distractorRationale.d: Only the salts the body needs are reabsorbed; the excess is excreted

questions.stem: Which components of blood are NOT found in the glomerular filtrate of a healthy kidney?

options.text: Red blood cells and plasma proteins

questions.explanation: Ultrafiltration works like a sieve based on molecular size. Blood cells and plasma proteins are far too large to pass through the capillary wall and the basement membrane, so they stay in the blood, while all the small molecules are forced through.

distractorRationale.a: Water and mineral salts are small and pass into the filtrate freely
distractorRationale.c: Both urea and glucose are small molecules that enter the filtrate, though glucose is later reabsorbed
distractorRationale.d: Amino acids and vitamins pass into the filtrate and are then reabsorbed

questions.stem: An increase in the secretion of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) results in

options.text: a large volume of dilute urine
a small volume of concentrated urine

questions.explanation: ADH makes the walls of the collecting ducts more permeable to water, so more water is reabsorbed into the blood as the filtrate passes through the salty medulla. Less water therefore leaves the body, and the urine that is produced is small in volume and dark.

distractorRationale.a: This is the result of low ADH, when the collecting ducts stay relatively impermeable
distractorRationale.c: Glucose in urine indicates diabetes mellitus, which involves insulin rather than ADH
distractorRationale.d: Protein in urine indicates damage to the filtering membrane

questions.stem: A farmer works all afternoon in the hot sun and sweats heavily without drinking. Which sequence describes his body's response?

options.text: Blood becomes more dilute, less ADH is released, and much dilute urine is produced
Blood becomes more concentrated, more ADH is released, and a small volume of concentrated urine is produced
Blood glucose falls, insulin is released, and glycogen is stored
Blood becomes more concentrated, ADH secretion stops, and water loss increases

questions.explanation: Sweating removes water and leaves the blood more concentrated. The hypothalamus detects the change and the pituitary releases more ADH, which raises the permeability of the collecting ducts so water is reabsorbed. The volume of urine falls, conserving water, and blood concentration returns towards normal.

distractorRationale.a: Sweating concentrates rather than dilutes the blood
distractorRationale.c: Insulin regulates glucose, not water balance
distractorRationale.d: Stopping ADH would increase water loss and worsen the dehydration; the response must cancel the change, not amplify it

questions.stem: When a person becomes too hot, which pair of responses helps to lower body temperature?

options.text: Increased sweating and vasodilation of skin arterioles
Erection of body hair and reduced sweating

questions.explanation: Evaporating sweat absorbs latent heat from the skin, and vasodilation brings more warm blood close to the surface so that heat is lost by radiation and conduction. Both responses increase the rate of heat loss.

distractorRationale.a: Shivering generates heat and vasoconstriction retains it, which are cold responses
distractorRationale.c: Erect hair traps insulating air and reduced sweating conserves heat
distractorRationale.d: Faster respiration would generate more heat, and vasoconstriction would trap it

questions.stem: Which hormone lowers blood glucose by causing the liver to convert glucose into glycogen?
questions.explanation: Insulin is secreted by the pancreas when blood glucose rises after a meal. It increases glucose uptake by cells and stimulates the liver to store the surplus as glycogen, so blood glucose falls back to normal.

distractorRationale.a: Glucagon does the opposite, converting glycogen back to glucose when blood sugar is low
distractorRationale.c: Adrenaline raises blood glucose as part of the response to fright or stress
distractorRationale.d: ADH regulates water reabsorption, not glucose

questions.stem: The presence of glucose in a person's urine is normal and shows that the kidney is filtering efficiently.
questions.explanation: False. Although glucose does enter the filtrate, a healthy proximal tubule reabsorbs all of it by active transport. Glucose in urine means the blood glucose was so high that the carriers were saturated, which is the classic sign of diabetes mellitus.

questions.stem: Homeostatic control in the body is described as negative feedback because the

options.text: response counteracts the original change and restores the normal level
body ignores small changes in the internal environment
hormones involved always reduce the rate of reactions

questions.explanation: In negative feedback, a departure from the set point triggers a response in the opposite direction. Rising blood glucose triggers insulin, which lowers it; a concentrated blood triggers ADH, which dilutes it. The corrective response then shuts down as the normal level is restored.

distractorRationale.a: Reinforcing a change is positive feedback, which would drive the system out of control
distractorRationale.c: Homeostatic systems are sensitive to small deviations, which is why levels stay narrow
distractorRationale.d: Some homeostatic hormones, such as glucagon and adrenaline, increase rates of reaction

questions.stem: Describe how urine is formed in a nephron, naming the two main processes involved. Explain what happens to the volume and concentration of urine when a person drinks two litres of water quickly.
markingGuide: Ultrafiltration: blood in the glomerulus is under high pressure because the outgoing arteriole is narrower than the incoming one, forcing water, glucose, amino acids, salts and urea into the Bowmans capsule while blood cells and plasma proteins remain in the blood (4 marks)

Selective reabsorption: all glucose and amino acids are reabsorbed by active transport in the proximal convoluted tubule, along with most mineral salts and much water by osmosis, leaving urea behind (4 marks)
Water conservation: the loop of Henle makes the medulla salty so water can be drawn out of the collecting duct by osmosis (1 mark)
Effect of drinking: the blood becomes more dilute, so the hypothalamus detects the fall in concentration and the pituitary releases less ADH (2 marks)

Consequence: the collecting ducts become less permeable to water, less water is reabsorbed, and a large volume of pale dilute urine is produced until the blood concentration returns to normal (2 marks)
questions.explanation: Urine formation must be presented as filtration followed by selective recovery, with the emphasis on why plasma proteins stay behind and why glucose does not. For the drinking scenario, the chain to trace is dilute blood, less ADH, less permeable collecting ducts, and therefore a large volume of dilute urine.

questions.stem: In the nephron, the process by which water is reabsorbed back into the bloodstream primarily occurs in the
questions.explanation: The collecting duct is where significant water reabsorption occurs, influenced by the presence of ADH. This process helps to concentrate the urine and maintain body fluid balance.

distractorRationale.a: The proximal convoluted tubule reabsorbs a large amount of water, but not as much as the collecting duct.
distractorRationale.b: The loop of Henle primarily reabsorbs salts and some water, but the majority of water reabsorption occurs later.
distractorRationale.c: The distal convoluted tubule does reabsorb some water, but the collecting duct is more critical for final water regulation.

questions.stem: What is the primary role of the hormone aldosterone in the process of osmoregulation?

options.text: Stimulates the reabsorption of sodium ions

questions.explanation: Aldosterone primarily stimulates the reabsorption of sodium ions in the nephron, which indirectly promotes water retention and helps regulate blood pressure. This is crucial for maintaining electrolyte balance and blood volume.

distractorRationale.a: While aldosterone influences water retention, its direct action is on sodium reabsorption.
distractorRationale.c: Aldosterone does promote potassium excretion, but its primary role in osmoregulation is sodium reabsorption.
distractorRationale.d: Aldosterone generally increases blood pressure through sodium and water retention, not reduces it.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best describes the role of ADH in the kidneys?

options.text: It promotes water reabsorption in the collecting duct
It stimulates the formation of urine

questions.explanation: ADH, or antidiuretic hormone, promotes the reabsorption of water in the collecting ducts of the kidneys, leading to more concentrated urine and reduced urine volume. This mechanism is vital for maintaining fluid balance in the body.

distractorRationale.a: ADH actually reduces urine volume by promoting water reabsorption.
distractorRationale.b: ADH increases, not decreases, water reabsorption.
distractorRationale.d: ADH does not stimulate the formation of urine; it affects how much water is reabsorbed.

questions.stem: Which part of the nephron is primarily responsible for selective reabsorption?
questions.explanation: The proximal convoluted tubule is where most selective reabsorption occurs, allowing the body to reclaim essential nutrients, electrolytes, and water from the filtrate. This process is crucial for maintaining homeostasis.

distractorRationale.a: The glomerulus is involved in filtration, not reabsorption.
distractorRationale.c: The loop of Henle plays a role in concentration but is not the primary site for selective reabsorption.
distractorRationale.d: The collecting duct is important for final adjustments but not for the initial selective reabsorption.

questions.stem: During extreme dehydration, the body responds by increasing the secretion of which hormone?
questions.explanation: In situations of extreme dehydration, the body increases the secretion of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) to promote water reabsorption in the kidneys, thus reducing urine output and conserving water.

distractorRationale.a: Insulin regulates blood glucose, not water balance.
distractorRationale.b: While aldosterone helps retain sodium and water, ADH is specifically responsible for water reabsorption.
distractorRationale.d: Glucagon primarily regulates glucose levels and does not play a role in hydration.

questions.stem: Which physiological process is primarily responsible for the concentration of urine?
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the key process that allows water to be reabsorbed from the filtrate in the nephron, particularly in the collecting duct, leading to the concentration of urine. This process is vital for maintaining the body's water balance.

distractorRationale.a: Filtration occurs at the glomerulus but does not concentrate urine.
distractorRationale.c: Active transport is involved in reabsorbing ions but not primarily in concentrating urine.
distractorRationale.d: Diffusion plays a role in various cellular processes but is not the main mechanism for urine concentration.

questions.stem: The structure that connects the kidney to the bladder is called the
questions.explanation: The ureter is the tube that connects each kidney to the bladder, allowing urine to flow from the kidney to be stored in the bladder before excretion. This anatomical feature is essential for the urinary system.

distractorRationale.a: The urethra carries urine from the bladder to the outside of the body.
distractorRationale.c: The renal pelvis is part of the kidney where urine collects before entering the ureter.
distractorRationale.d: The nephron is the functional unit of the kidney, not a structure connecting to the bladder.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the role of the loop of Henle in the nephron?
questions.explanation: The loop of Henle plays a crucial role in concentrating urine by creating a concentration gradient in the renal medulla, which facilitates the reabsorption of water and salts. This is key for the body's water conservation.

distractorRationale.a: Glucose reabsorption primarily occurs in the proximal convoluted tubule.
distractorRationale.c: Filtration occurs at the glomerulus, not in the loop of Henle.
distractorRationale.d: Waste products are secreted mainly in the distal convoluted tubule, not in the loop of Henle.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of the renal corpuscle in the nephron?
questions.explanation: The renal corpuscle, which consists of the glomerulus and Bowman's capsule, is primarily responsible for filtering blood to form glomerular filtrate. This is the first step in urine formation.

distractorRationale.a: Nutrient reabsorption occurs later in the nephron, not in the renal corpuscle.
distractorRationale.c: Hormones are not secreted at the renal corpuscle; they are involved in regulation elsewhere.
distractorRationale.d: While blood pressure can influence filtration, the renal corpuscle's main role is filtration, not regulation.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes how the body regulates temperature?

options.text: By reducing blood flow to the skin

questions.explanation: The body regulates temperature through mechanisms such as vasodilation, which increases blood flow to the skin, and sweating, which helps cool the body through evaporation. These processes are essential for maintaining homeostasis.

distractorRationale.a: Increasing metabolic rate generates heat rather than cooling the body.
distractorRationale.c: Reducing blood flow to the skin would increase body temperature, not regulate it.
distractorRationale.d: While respiration rate can increase during heat stress, it is not the primary method of temperature regulation.

questions.stem: In the nephron, the process of selective reabsorption primarily occurs in which structure?
questions.explanation: The proximal convoluted tubule is the primary site for selective reabsorption in the nephron, where essential nutrients, ions, and water are reabsorbed back into the bloodstream. This process ensures that vital substances are not lost in urine.

distractorRationale.a: The glomerulus is involved in filtration, not reabsorption.
distractorRationale.c: The distal convoluted tubule also participates in reabsorption but to a lesser extent than the proximal tubule.
distractorRationale.d: The collecting duct is involved in water reabsorption but is not the primary site for selective reabsorption.

questions.stem: Which of the following hormones increases water reabsorption in the kidneys?
questions.explanation: Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) increases water reabsorption in the kidneys by making the collecting ducts more permeable to water, thus reducing urine output and conserving water in the body. This is crucial for maintaining hydration levels.

distractorRationale.a: Aldosterone primarily regulates sodium reabsorption and potassium secretion.
distractorRationale.b: Adrenaline is involved in the fight or flight response and does not primarily affect water reabsorption.
distractorRationale.d: Insulin regulates blood glucose levels and does not have a direct role in water reabsorption.

questions.stem: What is the effect of a decrease in blood volume on the secretion of ADH?

options.text: ADH is secreted only in response to high blood pressure

questions.explanation: A decrease in blood volume triggers the hypothalamus to increase the secretion of ADH, which promotes water reabsorption in the kidneys, helping to restore blood volume and maintain blood pressure. This is a critical response to dehydration.

distractorRationale.b: A decrease in blood volume would not lead to decreased ADH; instead, it stimulates its release.
distractorRationale.c: ADH levels change in response to blood volume; they do not remain unchanged under these conditions.
distractorRationale.d: ADH is primarily secreted in response to low blood volume and high osmolarity, not just high blood pressure.

questions.stem: Which part of the nephron is responsible for the majority of water reabsorption?
questions.explanation: The proximal convoluted tubule is responsible for reabsorbing approximately 65-70% of the water filtered by the glomerulus. This is essential for maintaining fluid balance and preventing dehydration.

distractorRationale.b: The Loop of Henle contributes to water reabsorption but to a lesser extent than the proximal convoluted tubule.
distractorRationale.c: The distal convoluted tubule reabsorbs some water but is not the primary site.
distractorRationale.d: The collecting duct reabsorbs water under the influence of ADH but is not where most water reabsorption occurs.

questions.stem: The regulation of body temperature is an example of which type of feedback mechanism?
questions.explanation: The regulation of body temperature is an example of negative feedback because the body responds to changes in temperature by initiating processes that counteract the change, such as sweating to cool down or shivering to generate heat.

distractorRationale.a: Positive feedback amplifies changes rather than counteracting them, which is not the case in temperature regulation.
distractorRationale.c: Neutral feedback is not a recognized category in physiological processes.
distractorRationale.d: Cyclic feedback is not a standard term used in biological feedback mechanisms.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a waste product excreted by the kidneys?
questions.explanation: Urea is a waste product formed from the breakdown of proteins and is primarily excreted by the kidneys in urine. It is a key component of nitrogenous waste excretion.

distractorRationale.a: Glucose is usually reabsorbed and not excreted in healthy individuals.
distractorRationale.c: Amino acids are typically reabsorbed and not found in urine under normal conditions.
distractorRationale.d: Proteins are too large to be filtered through the glomerulus and are not excreted.

questions.stem: What role does the Loop of Henle play in urine concentration?

distractorRationale.b: Glucose reabsorption primarily occurs in the proximal convoluted tubule, not in the Loop of Henle.
distractorRationale.d: Urea is not secreted by the Loop of Henle; it is excreted in urine.

distractorRationale.c: Cortisol secretion is not directly related to immediate blood glucose regulation.
distractorRationale.d: Adrenaline may increase during stress but is not primarily involved in the regulation of low blood glucose levels.

questions.stem: Which of the following processes is primarily responsible for the removal of nitrogenous waste from the body?

distractorRationale.c: Digestion is the breakdown of food, not the excretion of waste.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of the renal tubule in the nephron?
questions.explanation: The renal tubule's primary function is the reabsorption of water, ions, and nutrients from the filtrate back into the bloodstream, as well as the secretion of additional waste products into the filtrate. This process is crucial for maintaining homeostasis in the body.

distractorRationale.a: Filtration occurs in the glomerulus, not in the renal tubule.
distractorRationale.c: Hormone secretion is not a primary function of the renal tubule.
distractorRationale.d: While urine is produced as a final product, the renal tubule's main role is in reabsorption and secretion.

questions.stem: Which process in the nephron allows for the selective reabsorption of essential ions and nutrients back into the bloodstream?
questions.explanation: Selective reabsorption is the process by which the nephron reabsorbs essential ions and nutrients from the filtrate back into the bloodstream. This process ensures that vital substances such as glucose, amino acids, and certain ions are retained while waste products are excreted.

distractorRationale.a: Filtration is the initial process where blood is filtered in the glomerulus, but it does not involve selective reabsorption.
distractorRationale.c: Secretion is the process of adding substances to the filtrate, not reabsorbing them back into the blood.
distractorRationale.d: Excretion refers to the removal of waste products from the body, which is the opposite of reabsorption.

questions.stem: What effect does high levels of ADH have on urine concentration?
questions.explanation: High levels of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) lead to increased water reabsorption in the kidneys, resulting in more concentrated urine. This mechanism is crucial for the body to conserve water during dehydration.

distractorRationale.a: Diluting urine occurs when there are low levels of ADH, allowing more water to be excreted.
distractorRationale.c: Increased urine volume is associated with low ADH levels, not high levels.
distractorRationale.d: ADH directly influences urine concentration, so it cannot have no effect.
